engagement_title: Apexguard rebrand rollout: recover the master mark off the only two objects it survives on, carry a dark house look across a bench and driveway shoot, and put a label on eighteen SKUs
vertical: Automotive aftermarket: paint protection film, window tint and installation hardware, sold to independent installers, Scottsdale, Arizona, master brand plus three sub brands
real_brief_anchor: Anchor, verbatim from the posted Upwork brief: the client "supplies paint protection film (PPF), window tint, and related products", is "rebranding and need a designer to deliver a complete logo and identity system that works on digital channels and physical packaging (boxes, labels, stickers)", with a visual direction of "Premium, modern, performance-automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory-catalog, not 'tuner.'", a "strong master + sub-brand naming" structure, and an explicit exclusion of "mascots, vintage badges, heavy gradients." The real post names no company, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Apexguard with coined sub brands Vantage, Umbra and Forge. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: drawing an identity from scratch is not connector work and the killed original sat almost entirely on a single imaging surface. What is genuinely doable, and is what this client actually needs on the day, is the rest of the same commission: the mark is RECOVERED from the two physical objects it still exists on rather than invented, the sub brand lockups are built by setting licensed type against that recovered mark, the packaging half becomes a real per SKU label run at one record per page, and the photography that has to carry the new look is graded, cut and placed rather than described. That is the honest fuller version of the posted job.
client_one_liner: Our mark only exists on a sticker and on a decal stuck to a shop window, our photography is a mess, and eighteen SKUs need labels for the new season.
client_brief:
Apexguard, rebrand rollout

We supply paint protection film, window tint and the hardware that goes with them, out of Scottsdale. Installers are our customers, and their customers see our boxes on the shelf behind the counter. We are rebranding under one master name with three sub brands: Vantage for film, Umbra for tint, Forge for hardware.

Here is our problem. Our mark exists on a die cut sticker and on a decal our first installer put on his shop glass, and nowhere else. The shop that drew it closed and took the files with it. We need the mark back as artwork we can put on a box, on a label, on a sticker the size of a thumbnail and on a banner, and it has to still be our mark rather than something new. It will sit mostly on our dark ground, and sometimes very small.

Our photography is a mess. Twelve parts shot on our own bench, six frames from a customer driveway including the only good shot of a finished car, two of those taken in the evening. We want a dark, expensive, confident look across all of it. Premium, modern, performance automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory catalog, not tuner. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.

Product pages are the exception: each part on plain white with nothing behind it, square, the part centred.

Then the labels. Eighteen SKUs, one label per SKU, each carrying its family, its sub brand, its fitment line, roll width and warranty term, with a picture of the part. Last year's label is attached exactly as it went to the printer. We need this year's run print ready, plus proofs to sign.

We also want a one page piece for the installer trade show and a set of posts, in one file we can edit ourselves.

Parts run two hundred fifty to twelve hundred dollars.
price_band_and_audience: Aftermarket film, tint and hardware at 250 to 1,200 dollars a line item, bought by independent installers aged 25 to 45 who resell to enthusiast end customers and who judge a supplier on whether the packaging looks like it belongs in a shop they are proud of. The band is load bearing in both directions. A dark, restrained, high contrast system with one accent reads as a supplier who is confident about margin, which is exactly what lets an installer justify the price to a customer standing at the counter. A 30 dollar universal accessory brand would correctly ship bright product on white with the price and the fitment shouting, and that treatment here makes the 1,200 dollar line item look overpriced. Push the other way into black on black minimalism with no fitment information and the installer cannot find the SKU on the shelf, which is a real operational failure, not a taste failure. The client's own exclusions, no mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients, are the guard rails against the tuner register that would drop the brand a band. A posted commission of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Built to sit behind the counter
brand_identity.sector: An automotive aftermarket supplier of paint protection film, window tint and installation hardware, sold to independent installers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Scottsdale, Arizona; a master brand rebranding over three sub brands, Vantage for film, Umbra for tint and Forge for hardware.
brand_identity.about: Apexguard supplies the film, tint and hardware that independent installers fit and resell to enthusiast owners. We are consolidating under one master name so the boxes on the shelf look like they belong in a shop the installer is proud of. The look is dark, modern and confident: premium performance, not tuner and not factory catalogue.
brand_identity.audience: Independent installers, 25 to 45, who judge a supplier on whether the packaging justifies the price to a customer standing at the counter.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Line items from two hundred fifty to twelve hundred dollars, a confident premium supplier rather than a bright discount accessory brand.
brand_identity.typography: A tight modern grotesque, mostly caps, with wide tracking on the master mark. Fitment and warranty lines are set plainly and stay legible at small size.
brand_identity.voice: Confident and terse, no hype. Example line: 'Film, tint and hardware. Fitted right, backed properly.' No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our master mark survives only on a die-cut box sticker and on a decal on an installer's shop glass. The studio that drew it has closed and taken the source files, so it has to be recovered as usable artwork.
brand_identity.values: A dark, high-contrast house system with one accent, where fitment information is always legible on the shelf. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.

assets_supplied.name: apexguard_bench/ (12 part frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Hardware and applicator parts photographed on the client's own charcoal workbench, one or two parts per frame, shot with a single overhead source.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we sell that is not a roll, shot on our bench the way we shoot everything."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Most of the parts are anodized black or gunmetal against a charcoal bench, so subject and ground share value along the machined flanks and a knockout returns a complete looking cutout that has quietly bitten into the flank of several parts. Three of the twelve frames are the same SKU at two rotations and one SKU has no bench frame at all.

assets_supplied.name: apexguard_installed/ (6 frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld frames from a customer driveway: film and tint on a finished car, two shot at dusk under street lighting, the rest in flat daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only good shot of a finished car is in here. Two of them were taken late."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The one frame carrying the whole flank is a near square capture that is off level, so a wide banner cannot be cropped from it without losing the flank, and any width has to be built rather than found. The two dusk frames sit two stops under with a sodium cast that a single global temperature move takes green on the paint while it is still correcting the concrete.

assets_supplied.name: apexguard_decal_glass.jpg and apexguard_box_sticker.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Two photographs of the surviving mark: a gloss vinyl decal on a curved shop window, and a die cut sticker on a matte box lid.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only two places the mark still exists. The shop that drew it closed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Neither is a scan. The decal is on curved glass under specular reflection, so the letterforms are subtly distorted and the ink runs close in value to the reflected sky at one corner, and the sticker was printed at thumbnail scale so ink spread has already partly filled its tightest counters on the object itself. Which of the two yields a mark that still holds at the size it actually reproduces on a label, and on a dark ground, is not knowable from either photograph.

assets_supplied.name: apexguard_label_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's box label exactly as it went to the printer: a single card with typeset blocks, a fitment line and a placed part photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The label as printed. This year's run should sit in the same footprint, we already bought the stock."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The fitment block is a fixed measure frame whose true measure is far shorter than the printed sample suggests, because the sample happened to carry the shortest fitment string in the range, and a merged record longer than that measure does not overset visibly, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge. The run still reports one page per row with no error and no warning.

assets_supplied.name: apexguard_skus.csv (18 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The season's range: SKU, product family, sub brand, fitment line, roll width, warranty term, and an image column naming the part picture.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Eighteen SKUs going on the shelf this season, exactly as our system exports them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The fitment lines range from twenty two to a hundred and ninety characters across the range, and two SKUs sit in a sub brand that has no label precedent anywhere in the supplied artwork.

assets_supplied.name: apexguard_brand_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the master and sub brand names, the house dark ground the boxes are printed on, the warranty wording legal approved, and the trade show stand dimensions.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Names, the ground colour we print boxes on, and the warranty wording we cannot change."

acceptance_bar: The recovered mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, genuinely scalable with a real viewBox present, and with no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it.

The mark still reads as the same mark at the size it actually reproduces on a label and on a thumbnail sticker, on the house dark ground, not merely at full canvas on white. A mark whose counters close at small size fails even if the large version is beautiful.
Three sub brand lockups exist that are the same recovered mark set against licensed type, consistent in relationship and spacing across all three, not three separate designs.

All six product-part cutouts, one per SKU that has a genuine isolatable bench part frame, sit on plain white, square at 2000 x 2000 px, the part centred with clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds along the machined flanks at full resolution rather than at preview scale. The twelve SKUs with no isolatable part are documented in the SKU reconciliation rather than forced onto white.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no crop or resize tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
The bench and driveway frames read as one dark house look: one black point, one white point, one warmth. The two dusk frames are brought to the set or named, not shipped at eighty percent.
The banner reads as one photograph. Any width that was built rather than found sits at the same black point and warmth as the rest and does not introduce anything the shot does not contain.

The label run is one print ready file with exactly one label per SKU row, in row order, each carrying its own family, sub brand, fitment line, roll width and warranty term, with a picture of its own part.
Every fitment line is fully present on its label. A label whose fitment line stops mid sentence at the frame edge is the failure this bar exists to catch, and it fails the whole run.
The look holds the client's own exclusions: no mascot, no vintage badge, no heavy gradient, and nothing that reads as tuner rather than as supplier.

The trade show piece and the post set live in ONE working file, each canvas keeping its own size, delivered with the self contained source, with live text in one type system and the mark as real vector rather than a picture of it.
The note records the recovery route and why, the grade parameters per frame, every resize any tool reported, the SKU reconciliation, and anything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background transparent and backgroundColor, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence, image_generative_expand with seeds, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision plus the recovery of the identity itself. It sets one dark house target and corrects eighteen frames toward it one call at a time, confines the dusk corrections so the paint does not go green while the concrete is fixed, cuts the parts onto white where subject and bench share value, builds the width the banner needs on the one frame that carries the flank, and recovers the master mark at ink level off two photographed objects with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform: a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge template authoring, data merge and press render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template with params.mappingJson as a JSON string, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout at resolution 300 with createSeparateFiles
adobe_surfaces.role: The packaging half of the posted brief, delivered as the only thing the connector actually does at volume: eighteen labels, one record per page, reverse engineered from last year's printed label into a live merge template, with each row binding a picture of its own part. It is also where the fitment field meets a frame with a real measure for the first time, at press resolution, on stock the client has already bought.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search on CCAsset, asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The trade show piece and the post set as one native editable document at mixed canvas sizes, and the only surface where the recovered mark and the licensed type meet as live objects rather than as pixels. The mark goes in as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored from the top left, every photograph is carried as embedded image data because a reference to a URL arrives as an empty grey box at full success, and each root declares its own canvas.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type half of the identity system, which is the part of the posted brief that is genuinely authorable here: a master and three sub brand wordmarks set against the recovered mark, plus the label and trade show hierarchy. The recommender refuses to pair, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction against premium performance automotive that is explicitly not tuner. Numeric weights are non standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unlaundered name discards the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset using short queries and a contentType filter and never an orientation filter, asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the installer bay atmosphere band the trade show piece needs and that no customer driveway frame can supply, IP clean, at camera scale, with generative technology candidates excluded and nothing showing a real vehicle badge. The Boards half persists the direction the owner signs off from, placed within the per call cap, with a partial result read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which half of the posted brief lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The identity cannot be drawn here, so the commission has to be re read as recovery plus type plus placement. The label run is genuine record per page variable data, the trade show piece needs an authored fixed canvas document, and everything else is raster. Naming that split up front is the difference between a deliverable set and a pile of images.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role and its SKU.
trajectory.judgement: The range file, the bench frames and the label all refer to the same SKUs under different names, so the manifest has to be keyed by SKU rather than by filename or the image binding later has nothing to stand on.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and SKU.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen photographs and both mark objects and triage them: which bench frames duplicate a SKU, which SKU has no frame, which driveway frames are dusk, which single frame carries the whole flank, and what condition each of the two surviving marks is actually in.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts twelve parts for eighteen SKUs and one good car shot. Only the pictures settle which SKUs are covered, and the two mark objects are different problems, one distorted by a curved substrate and one already compromised by print at size.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note plus a written read on both mark objects.

trajectory.action: Level what is off level, before any crop or width decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: The banner frame is off level and straightening reframes it and eats edge pixels, so it must happen before anything is decided about how much width has to be built.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix the dark house target off the cleanest daylight frame and correct each of the eighteen frames toward it with its own call, recording every parameter applied.
trajectory.judgement: Dark is a decision about black point and warmth, not an exposure move, and the client's exclusions rule out the gradient heavy register that usually stands in for it. One batched call applies one identical parameter set across a bench, a driveway and a dusk street, which is exactly wrong.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine the corrections on the two dusk frames, selecting the affected material by its own visual properties rather than by the object it belongs to.
trajectory.judgement: A single global temperature move that neutralises the concrete takes the paint green, and prompt wording is the entire gate, since naming the car pulls the selection to the whole vehicle rather than to the surface that is casting wrong.
trajectory.produces: Two dusk frames brought toward the set, or a written reason one of them cannot be.

trajectory.action: Cut the parts out for the product pages onto plain white and to transparency, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message, and inspecting each cut edge at full resolution against white and against the house dark ground.
trajectory.judgement: Anodized black against a charcoal bench gives subject detection almost nothing to work with along a machined flank, so the cheap route and the material selection route have to be triaged per part rather than chosen once for the batch.
trajectory.produces: Six white ground plates and their transparent variants, one for each SKU that has a genuine isolatable bench part frame, with tradeoff records transcribed and edges inspected; the SKUs with no isolatable part recorded for the SKU reconciliation rather than forced onto white.

trajectory.action: Cut the square product tiles with the part optically centred and clear air at every edge.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on an applicator with a handle running off one side, and the client's page rejects anything touching the edge.
trajectory.produces: Six product tiles at spec, each 2000 x 2000 px square.

trajectory.action: Recover the master mark: choose which of the two objects to work from, select at ink level by naming the mark's own visual properties, set the polarity, crop from the selection's own bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox and remove the opaque full canvas ground path. Produce the colour accurate plate variant as well.
trajectory.judgement: Four decisions the tools do not make: which object, how to word the selection so it takes the ink rather than the glass or the box lid, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate knockout plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on a mark with enclosed counters.
trajectory.produces: A transparent scalable master mark and a colour accurate variant, both with the ground path stripped.

trajectory.action: Place the recovered mark at the size it actually reproduces on a label and on a thumbnail sticker, on the house dark ground, and look at it there.
trajectory.judgement: A mark is judged at reproduction size on the real ground, never at full canvas on white. This is the only place the recovery can be accepted or rejected.
trajectory.produces: A judgement on the recovered mark at its two real sizes on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Produce the sub brand colourways from the accepted mark using the same mask with different parameters, reporting what was dialed for each.
trajectory.judgement: Three sub brands need three readable states of one mark, not three marks, and the range that survives a hue move is moderate, so a sub brand that needs a far apart colour has to be reached by value rather than by hue.
trajectory.produces: Three sub brand states of one mark with the parameters recorded per state.

trajectory.action: Build the banner from the one frame that carries the whole flank: expand the short axis with a recorded seed, then crop to the banner ratio, reading the returned tradeoff record, and inspect the built region beside the graded set.
trajectory.judgement: The frame is near square and the flank is the whole point, so width has to be built rather than cropped in. The built region is the only part of the deliverable that no photographer took, so it has to be judged against the shot rather than against plausibility.
trajectory.produces: A banner candidate with its seed and tradeoff record, inspected beside the graded set.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the installer bay atmosphere band, filter to photography, exclude generative technology candidates and anything showing a real vehicle badge, then license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the dark target rather than the strongest thumbnail, and remember the thumbnail is all that exists before licensing. Long queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale atmosphere frame graded into the house target.

trajectory.action: Convert last year's label to a working document, export the interchange format, and inspect what the conversion actually exposed: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, their real bounds, and the true story text reassembled from its runs.
trajectory.judgement: The printed label is not evidence of its own structure, and the frame bounds that matter are the converted ones, not the ones the printed sample implies.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory with bounds, and the reconstructed story text held as the basis for every offset.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the reconstructed story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, then round trip the document again and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation and a success message report intent, not outcome. The only proof a placeholder landed is finding it in the round tripped document, which no tool asks for.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been confirmed rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Merge the range to one print ready file at one label per row, binding each row's own part picture through the image column, then merge again to a working document, render signing proofs at print resolution, and read the proofs record by record including the longest fitment lines.
trajectory.judgement: The image column is why the cutouts exist and a naive run puts one static picture on every label. Reading the first and last proof is not reading the run, because the records that stress a frame are not at the ends.
trajectory.produces: A print ready label run at one label per row, plus per label proofs at print resolution, read record by record.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction, judged against premium performance automotive that is explicitly not factory catalog and not tuner. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role, and the three sub brand wordmarks set.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained document carrying the trade show piece and the post set at their own canvas sizes, with the mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored from the top left, every photograph carried as embedded image data, and family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is holding the client's exclusions while still reading premium on a trade show floor.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document, retained as the durable half of the deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, verify the first canvas from the rendition and the rest from the returned per canvas markup, then create the selects board, add the graded set, the tiles and the licensed frame within the per call cap re sending only failed entries, and write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition shows only the first artboard, so looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable. A partial board result is reported as a success, so the failed list is the only honest count, and vector cannot go on a board so the mark belongs in the note instead.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with a per canvas audit, a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it is actually printed. Both source objects were traced from photographs, and the tracing tool takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster preparation. A trace that is clean, complete and correct at full canvas can close its tightest counters once it is set at label size, and the closure is worse on the house dark ground than on white because a filled counter and a solid stroke become one shape. Whether it happens, and to which letterforms, depends on this object's ink spread, this photograph's contrast and this trace's path simplification, none of which are reported anywhere.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Nothing avoids it by ordering, because the artwork must exist before it can be set at reproduction size, and the tracing tool exposes no threshold, no colour count and no simplification control that could be set correctly in advance. Nothing in the brief states it: the client says only that the mark will sit small and on a dark ground, which is a requirement rather than a disclosure. The response is not the same call again but a different upstream route, re preparing the raster with a tighter ink level selection, switching to the other surviving object, or reversing the mark so it is knocked out light on the dark ground, which changes which counters have to survive at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re run the recovery from the alternate object or with a differently prepared raster, re inject the viewBox and re strip the ground path, re judge at both real sizes on the real ground rather than at full canvas, and then re derive the three sub brand states from whichever mark was actually accepted.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rebrand shipped on boxes, labels and thumbnail stickers where the master mark is a dark blob on a dark ground at every size the customer actually sees it, with the only version that reads being the one in the presentation.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every fitment line actually fits. The label's fitment block is a fixed measure frame, and the printed sample carries the shortest fitment string in the range, so the printed page is actively misleading about the frame's real measure. On the longer records the merged text does not overset visibly and raises nothing: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, mid word, while the run still returns one page per row with no error, no warning and no overset flag. The truncation point is a property of the converted frame's bounds, which the printed label does not disclose.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it because the frame's real measure only exists after the conversion and only bites once real data is flowed into it, and the record range spans twenty two to a hundred and ninety characters, so the failure appears only on records that are not at either end of the file. Nothing states it: the client says the run should sit in the same footprint because the stock is bought, which is a constraint, not a warning. The response is a decision about the data and the mapping, moving the fitment field to a frame with real measure, splitting it, or applying the abbreviation the client's own approved wording permits, not merging the same mapping again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every proof rather than the first and the last, identify which records truncate, re decide where the fitment field lives or how it is written, rebuild the mapping against the reconstructed story text, re confirm the placeholders in the round tripped document, then re merge and re render and read the proofs again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen labels printed on stock the client has already bought, on which the SKUs with the longest fitment lines, which are exactly the ones an installer most needs to check, stop mid sentence at the edge of the block.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the width the banner needs can be built at all on this frame. The only capture carrying the whole flank is near square, so the banner cannot be cropped from it and the short axis has to be extended, which is the one generative operation available. What the extension actually produces is invisible until it is run and looked at: it may continue the body line into a shape the car does not have, invent a second arch or a reflection of a sky the shot does not contain, and it builds those pixels from a neighbourhood whose black point and warmth may not match the graded set once the two sit side by side at banner width. The call returns success and a plausible image either way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because expanding before grading and expanding after grading both leave the same question open, namely whether the invented content is truthful to this vehicle, and no parameter controls that. Nothing states it: the brief says only that this is the one good shot of a finished car. The response is a decision rather than a re run, either accept the built width, reduce the banner ambition to what the frame genuinely carries, or re plan the banner around a different frame that has width but not the flank, each of which changes the trade show piece.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the built region beside the graded set at banner width rather than at preview scale, decide whether to keep, retreat to a narrower banner, or rebuild the piece around a different frame, then re compose the trade show canvas around whichever survives and re state in the note that a region of that image was built rather than photographed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A trade show banner two metres wide in which the client's own customer's car has an extra arch or a seam of different black at the join, presented to installers as the flagship example of the client's work.

deliverables.name: Apexguard master mark and sub brand lockups
deliverables.spec: The master mark recovered from the two objects it survives on, delivered as placeable scalable artwork with a transparent ground, a real viewBox present and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, in a single colour form and a colour accurate variant, holding at label size and at thumbnail sticker size on the house dark ground as well as reversed on light. Plus three sub brand states of that same mark for Vantage, Umbra and Forge, produced from one mask with recorded parameters, consistent in relationship and spacing rather than three separate designs.

deliverables.name: Apexguard house photography, bench, driveway and banner

decision_gates: How to re read a posted identity brief when the identity cannot be drawn: what recovery, type and placement can honestly deliver, and what has to be said plainly to the client instead.
Which of the two surviving objects to recover the mark from, given one is distorted by a curved substrate and the other was already compromised by print at size.
How to word the ink level selection so it takes the mark rather than the glass, the reflected sky or the box lid, and which polarity to trace.
Whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate plate is the deliverable, judged at reproduction size on the house dark ground rather than at full canvas.
Whether to reverse the mark on the dark ground, which changes entirely which counters have to survive.
How to reach three sub brand states from one mark when the hue range available is moderate, and when to move value instead of hue.
Cut route per part: the cheap route for a part that separates from the bench versus a material named bench selection inverted and filled for an anodized part whose flank shares value with the ground.
Whether to build width on the banner frame at all, and whether what gets built is truthful to that car or has to be abandoned for a narrower banner.
How to correct two dusk frames without taking the paint green while neutralising the concrete, and when to name a frame rather than save it.
Where the fitment field can live given the converted frame's real measure and a range spanning twenty two to a hundred and ninety characters, and which approved abbreviation is acceptable.
How to report eighteen SKUs against twelve bench frames with duplicates, one missing part and two SKUs whose sub brand has no precedent, without quietly choosing for the client.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against premium performance automotive that is explicitly not factory catalog and not tuner.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome new automotive logo and some dark car photography. IDENTITY: the client is not asking for a mark, they are asking for THEIR mark, which exists only on a decal and a sticker and must be recovered rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different company's logo and every box, label and sticker already in the field would stop matching. The parts are the client's actual SKUs and the car is the client's actual customer's car. SPEC: six product tiles at an exact 2000 x 2000 px square size with air at every edge and no interpolated pixels, one for each SKU that actually has an isolatable part, and a label run with exactly one page per range row in row order, in last year's footprint, on stock already bought, each label carrying its own fitment line in full, is not something a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the trade show piece and the post set exist to be edited between shows by a supplier with no designer. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: does this trace hold at nine millimetres on a dark ground, does this cutout have an edge along the flank, does this fitment line reach its last word.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING AND RECOVERY: the extract and reuse chain of select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area and vectorize is verified live end to end, including a stroke level mask of a printed mark on a photographed object with letter counters correctly excluded, and a full colour plate route that preserved brand hues. The vector hygiene the acceptance bar scores is exactly what the audit records the tool NOT doing: vectorize emits no viewBox and always writes a full canvas opaque rectangle at path index zero, and it takes no options at all, so the raster preparation is the only lever, which is what makes the reproduction size checkpoint a real decision rather than a parameter. remove_background is documented as unable to punch enclosed interiors and as collapsing on disjoint lettering, which is why the recovery route is selection based. Masked hue moves are verified at moderate range, which is why the sub brand gate is written as states rather than as named colours. generative_expand is verified live at up to 4096 pixels a side with seeds for reproducibility and is the single sanctioned generative call. crop_and_resize is verified to report upscaling only inside its tradeoffs array, which is what the no enlargement gate is checked against. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template with mappingJson passed as a JSON string, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous; one record per page for PDF output is verified with page count equal to row count in correct order; per row image binding through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually; 300 DPI raster requires merging to InDesign then rendering, which the trajectory does; and frame granularity from a converted PDF is documented as not under the author's control, which is why the true bounds are inspected before anything is promised. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, photographs must be embedded because every external URL resolved to a placeholder at full success, an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right is documented as breaking, and the rendition preview is first artboard only. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including non standard numeric weights per family and the all or nothing kit call. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, licensing verified at camera scale, boards capped at twelve placements per call with 201 meaning partial and vector unsupported, which the handover accounts for. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate on a PDF derived template, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no generative fill, no AI object removal, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above 20.
